title: Strings, Runes & Type Conversions
intro: Strings in Go work differently from Python or Java, and every fresher interview includes at least one string question. This module covers string immutability in Go (a string is a read-only slice of bytes — you cannot modify it in place), the distinction between byte (uint8, raw bytes) and rune (int32, a Unicode code point — ranging over a string with range gives runes, not bytes), safe string iteration with range (iterates runes), the strings package for common operations (strings.Contains, strings.Split, strings.TrimSpace, strings.Builder for efficient concatenation), strconv for converting between strings and numbers (strconv.Atoi, strconv.Itoa, strconv.ParseFloat), explicit type conversion with T(x) syntax (Go has no implicit numeric conversions), and type assertions for interface values. The gotcha question: 'why does len("café") return 5 instead of 4?' — this module answers it and explains why.
